fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (18.5x on ~$4.75 NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 = $88), FCF yield (5% on ~$4.26/sh FY28 FCF over 575M shares = $85) and EV/EBITDA (14x ~$3.26B FY28 EBITDA less ~$3.8B Sep-2027 net debt, over 575M shares = $73). Weights 0.45/0.30/0.25 give ~$83.4, rounded to $84. All three methods now use the same 575M share base.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Bottom-up FY28 (Mar-2028): revenue ~$7.4B (consensus $7.43B), non-GAAP GM ~65.5%, operating margin ~40% = ~$2.96B, interest ~$180M, non-GAAP tax ~8% (Q1 FY27 actual ~7.5%), 575M non-GAAP diluted shares = ~$4.45. Consensus FY28 is $4.58. NTM EPS at Sep-2027 (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) rolls forward half a year of growth to ~$4.85 unhaircut; I use ~$4.75 (a ~2% cycle haircut). 18.5x, the low end of the mid-cycle range, reflecting leverage and 5%+ 10-yr yields (peers: NXPI ~15x, ON ~24x, TXN/ADI ~28-32x).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~$2.45B (33% FCF margin on $7.4B, in line with Q1 FY27's 33.5%) / 575M shares including the 23.8M mandatory-convertible shares = ~$4.26/sh; 5.0% required FCF yield (ON ~4.9%, NXPI ~4.7%, plus a leverage premium)

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 adj. EBITDA ~$3.26B (44% of $7.4B) x 14x = $45.6B EV; less ~$3.8B net debt at Sep-2027 ($5.09B at Jun-2026 less ~$250-300M/qtr paydown after ~$275M/qtr common + preferred dividends) = $41.8B / 575M shares

bear.story: The upcycle peaks in mid-2027 after ~8 quarters. Industrial/auto orders roll over as customers pull back from buffers built during the lead-time stretch; GM drifts from 66-67% toward ~61-62% as utilization falls, and the market prices a FY29 decline. Semis multiples compress further with 5%+ Treasury yields. NTM EPS ~$3.45 x 15x. The mandatory convertible adds dilution below ~$62.5.

base.story: Recovery continues at a slower pace: FY28 revenue ~$7.4B, GM holds ~65-66% (the through-cycle model is 65%; guided 66-67% into December), op margin ~40%, data center/PCIe Gen6 ramps in 2027, net debt reaches ~$3.8B and net leverage falls toward ~2x. NTM EPS ~$4.75 x 18.5x.

bull.story: A full cyclical upturn toward the FY23 peak (~$8.4B revenue run-rate): price increases stick, operating margin moves above the 40% through-cycle model (company target per Citi TMT 2026-09-09; corrected from 45% by the citation gate), data center grows past $1.5B, buybacks restart on the $1.56B authorization once leverage is low, and the multiple re-rates to ~21x on ~$5.7 NTM EPS.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$55 (about -30%, ~12x FY28 consensus EPS of $4.58), the market would be pricing an outright reversal: book-to-bill below 1, a guidance cut with GM falling back toward 60%, and distributor inventory rebuilding from its lean 25 days. That is not ordinary 50%-vol sector noise. Below ~$62.5 the mandatory convertible preferred also converts into more shares (up to ~29M below ~$51), adding dilution to a falling price.

catalysts.event: Q2 FY27 results (guide $1.589-1.618B revenue, 66-67% GM, $0.91-0.95 EPS) and December-quarter guide; first full quarter of the price increase
Q3 FY27 results; March-quarter guide; whether GM holds ~66% after the one-time licensing and repricing boosts roll off
Q4 FY27 results and FY28 outlook; possible capital-return update as net leverage falls
Q1 FY28 results; PCIe Gen6 / NVMe data-center ramps; first signs of whether the upcycle is maturing
Fed and Treasury-yield path (10-yr ~5.1%) and US-China tariff/trade negotiations
Hailo edge-AI integration (closed 2026-09-21) and possible further tuck-in M&A

key_uncertainties: Timing of the cycle peak: near-term channel is lean (distributor inventory 25 days, no double ordering per the CFO), but by mid-2027 the upcycle is ~8 quarters old and the market will be pricing FY29
Gross-margin sustainability after one-time licensing and distributor-repricing gains; the price increase and lower underutilization charges are supposed to offset
Valuation multiple under 5%+ 10-yr yields and the sector de-rating since the July-2026 AI selloff
Foundry/OSAT advanced-packaging capacity constraints limiting data-center shipments
Pace of deleveraging (~$250-300M/qtr after dividends) versus the restart of buybacks; CEO 10b5-1 selling
Industrial and automotive recovery lagging data center and aerospace/defense
reasoning: Round 2. Fundamentals are improving: Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue was $1.485B (+38% y/y), non-GAAP OM 35.1%, EPS $0.76 (beat). The Q2 guide is $1.59-1.62B, GM 66-67% and EPS $0.91-0.95, which would be the seventh straight quarter above seasonal. The supervisor's corrections, which I verified against the Q1 press release, apply to my inputs: (1) all methods now use 575M non-GAAP diluted shares, because the 23.8M mandatory-convertible shares are certain to convert in Mar-2028; (2) non-GAAP tax is ~7.5-8%, not 13% (Q1: op income $521M, net income $439M); (3) net debt was $5.09B and fell only ~$170M in the June quarter after ~$247M of common dividends, so I use ~$3.8B at Sep-2027, not $4.5B. That also fixes my internal inconsistency; (4) the 175 days I cited is company inventory; distributor inventory is a lean 25 days. The lower tax rate lifts EPS; FY28 consensus is $4.58, revised up from $4.19. I roll forward to ~$4.75 NTM at Sep-2027 but cut the multiple to 18.5x. The mandatory-convertible shares and the rate backdrop make me unwilling to pay 19x on a higher EPS near a maturing cycle. The share-base fix lowers the FCF leg ($87 to $85). The EV/EBITDA leg barely moves ($74 to $73): the lower net debt is offset by moving from 550M to 575M shares. The supervisor expected $77-78, but on my own inputs (14x, 575M shares) I get $73. The blend is unchanged at ~$84; the corrections largely offset. I cut the bear weight from 25% to 20% and raised the bear price to $52, since the lean channel and flat GM guidance make a reversal within the next 2-3 quarters less likely. I do not go lower, because the risk shifts to mid-2027, inside the horizon. Scenario mean is ~$88.6 and median ~$85-86. Ladder: a lognormal centered on an ~$85 median with 40% sigma, the left tail fattened slightly for a cycle reversal and convertible dilution. P(>= spot $78.69) is ~0.57. Sell-side views remain wide (Cantor $125 Overweight; Truist cut to $90 Hold). Research used web search only (2 extra searches this round); no option data was consulted.
